tip: пока не (poka ne) here means until; the не carries no negation, so стемнело (stemnelo = got dark) still happened.
пока (poka) with no не (ne) means while, two things happening at once: Пока мы ехали (poka my ehali = while we drove).
в том (v tom) literally means in that; it is a fixed frame pointing ahead to the clause after the comma, as in Вопрос в том (vopros v tom = the question is).
без (bez = without) always forces the genitive case, which is why kind people appears as добрых людей (dobryh lyudej).
как только (kak tolko) means as soon as; Russian uses the future here, сможет (smozhet = will be able), where English says could.
чтобы (chtoby) plus an infinitive like читать (chitat = to read) means in order to, used when one subject does both actions.
Куда бы (kuda by) with ни (ni) means wherever, no matter where; the pair бы ни wraps the whole clause.
Несмотря на то что (nesmotrya na to chto) is a fixed phrase for despite the fact that, used before a full clause with a verb like шёл (shyol = was falling).
так (tak) plus что frames so... that: так тихо (tak tiho = so quiet), then что (chto) introduces the result.
и (i) repeated before each item means both... and: и красивая, и умная, и добрая (i krasivaya, i umnaya, i dobraya).
две (dve = two) takes the genitive singular, so беда (beda) shifts to беды (bedy) after it, not the plural.
